cita: Sun et al. (2026). OpsMem: Dual-Memory Reasoning with Cross-Memory Resonance for Failure Diagnosis.
problema: LLM-based failure diagnosis needs iterative evidence acquisition guided by operational experience, but existing agentic-reasoning methods suffer long-horizon instability over linear context while knowledge-augmented (RAG) methods retrieve operational experience statically, without continuously aligning it to the evolving diagnostic state.
mecanismo: OpsMem maintains two graph-structured memories: a short-term memory (STM) capturing the current incident's evolving belief state (symptoms/evidence/hypotheses linked by derive/refine/support/refute edges) and a long-term memory (LTM) of cross-incident patterns/cases/procedures. Cross-Memory Resonance (signal coupling -> pattern activation -> memory propagation) activates the LTM subgraph most relevant to the current STM at every round, jointly conditioning a multi-agent diagnosis loop (Central Agent plans, Expert Agents acquire/analyze evidence, STM is updated); after resolution, a multi-agent consolidation module (MetaAgent + memory agents) proposes CREATE/DELETE node operations to distill the solved incident back into the LTM.
evaluacion: 120 real-world Huawei microservice failure incidents, LLM-as-a-Judge (Match/Relevant on a 3-point scale) across three seed LLMs, against ReAct, GoS, and GoS+VectorRAG/GraphRAG/LinearRAG baselines, with an ablation removing STM/LTM/CMR/LTM-consolidation and a sequential-window self-evolution study.
numeros_clave: OpsMem improves Match by 6.66-25.00 points and Relevant by 3.33-13.33 points over the strongest baseline per seed LLM (e.g. Qwen3.5-27B: Match 78.33 vs GoS+LinearRAG 53.33, Relevant 85.83 vs 72.50); ablation shows removing LTM causes the largest drop (Match 78.33->30.83); self-evolution study shows growing gains vs a fixed-LTM variant across four incident windows (+0/+3/+1/+5 Match).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The short-term memory is an explicit graph-structured belief state of the current diagnostic task (symptoms/evidence/hypotheses with derive/refine/support/refute relations, §III-A), a concrete instance of plan/task state as first-class memory that is read/updated every reasoning round.

An ablation directly measures that removing Cross-Memory Resonance (state-aware LTM activation) hurts performance versus always retrieving generically (Table II, w/o CMR row), evidence that state-conditioned retrieval design is measurably load-bearing, reinforcing ADR-019.

A dedicated multi-agent consolidation module (MetaAgent reviews CREATE/DELETE proposals before merging, §III-D) gates promotion of solved-incident experience into durable long-term memory, and the self-evolution study (Table III) shows this measurably compounds over time -- confirming MF's deliberate-promotion stance.

notes: Table I (main results, 3 seed LLMs) and Table II-III (ablation, self-evolution windows) anchor the numbers; Fig.5 shows a worked case study of cross-memory resonance on a real incident.

cita: Huang, Z., Gutierrez, S., Kamana, H. y MacNeil, S. (2023). Memory Sandbox: Transparent and Interactive Memory Management for Conversational Agents.
problema: LLM-powered conversational agents manage conversational memory (summarization, selective storage, retrieval) entirely behind the interface, so users lack any affordance for viewing or controlling what the agent remembers, producing a poor mental model and conversational breakdowns when the agent's and the user's understanding of 'what was said' diverge.
mecanismo: Memory Sandbox reifies conversational history as draggable, editable 'memory objects' in a 2D-canvas UI: users can toggle a memory object's visibility (hide/show what the agent 'sees'), edit or delete an object to refine or remove context, add new objects to supplement context, select and summarize a group of objects into a new distilled object, and drag-copy objects by reference across separate conversations/agents to share context between them.
evaluacion: A design-probe system (Next.js + GPT-3.5-turbo) presented with a walkthrough of its interaction affordances and discussed qualitatively against explainable-AI and common-ground literature; the authors explicitly defer formal user studies of efficacy/trade-offs to future work.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Treating each memory entry as an inspectable, editable object that a human can view/edit/delete directly (§2.1-2.3) is an early, direct precursor of MF's 'docs=truth, typed and human-legible' stance, applied to conversational memory instead of project docs.

The paper's core motivation is that a hidden memory-management strategy causes a 'poor mental model' and breakdowns for the user (§1); making memory state transparent and directly manipulable is presented as the fix, supporting MF's concern that opaque memory erodes trust/provenance.

Summarization is a user-triggered, selective operation over chosen memory objects rather than an automatic background process (§2.4), an alternative human-in-the-loop consolidation trigger MF could consider alongside fully automated promotion.

notes: This is an HCI design-probe/vision paper (CHI-style short paper, 2023) with only a system walkthrough and no quantitative evaluation (evidencia_tipo=CUALITATIVA only, hence numeros_clave=NINGUNO); the earliest paper in this batch (predates most cited memory-system work it inspired).

cita: Jiang et al. (2026). RepLLM: Toward Automatically Reproducing Network Research Results.
problema: Reproducing network-systems research code from papers is hard because open-source implementations are rare (only ~38% of SIGCOMM/NSDI papers over the past decade ship code) and general-purpose multi-agent code-generation frameworks suffer excessive redundant token consumption, ambiguous task allocation, and lack verification/error-recovery when generating long, interdependent multi-file codebases.
mecanismo: RepLLM coordinates four specialized agents (Content Parsing, Architecture Design, Code Generation, Audit & Repair) through an explicit file-system-backed Shared Memory: a dedicated shared_memory directory holding structured JSON ground-truth artifacts (paper.json, appendix.json) that is excluded from LLM prompts by default, governed by a rule-based read-write protocol under a stateless LLM-API interface (no dialogue history carried across calls). The Architecture Design Agent decomposes the target system into a DAG of operational steps with explicit I/O interfaces (the reproduction plan) stored in Shared Memory, and a sandbox-isolated hierarchical refinement loop (static analysis then execution-trace-driven debugging) iteratively repairs the generated code.
evaluacion: Evaluation on representative SIGCOMM/NSDI network-systems papers against SOTA system-level LLM code-generation frameworks (e.g. Claude Code CLI, broadcast-style multi-agent baselines), measuring compile-readiness, logical correctness and fidelity of reproduction against official implementations plus token consumption.
numeros_clave: Reproduces 95% of the original benchmarks within approximately two hours; reduces token consumption by up to 10% vs SOTA baselines; contrasted against a reported >10 million tokens for Claude Code CLI to generate a thousand-line codebase (Section 2.3.2); only 38.05% of SIGCOMM/NSDI papers over the past decade ship open-source code (motivating statistic).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The Architecture Design Agent's DAG-of-operational-steps decomposition, with explicit per-step I/O interfaces stored in Shared Memory and consumed by later agents (Section 3.1.2), is a concrete plan-state artifact treated as first-class shared memory across the pipeline.

An explicit filesystem-backed Shared Memory (paper.json as ground truth, isolated from ordinary prompts) rather than implicit per-agent context or broadcast is exactly MF's single-source-per-fact stance, and the paper attributes its token-efficiency gains directly to this design versus AutoGen-style broadcast (Section 2.3.2).

Reports up to 10% token-consumption reduction vs SOTA baselines and contrasts this against a reported >10M-token cost for a naive multi-agent baseline (Claude Code CLI) on a 1K-LOC codebase, hard evidence for MF's context-economy stance.

notes: Abstract and Section 2.3.2/5.2 (Shared-Memory design and token-consumption comparison) anchor the numbers; pdftotext produced OCR/encoding syntax-error noise on this PDF but the main prose was recoverable.

cita: Chen et al. (2025). Multi-LLM Orchestration for High-Quality Code Generation: Exploiting Complementary Model Strengths.
problema: In single-LLM code-generation pipelines, no one model dominates across all programming languages, algorithmic problem categories, or generation/debugging/refinement stages, so committing to one fixed model throughout the pipeline leaves measurable code-quality gains unexploited.
mecanismo: PerfOrch decomposes generation into four agents (Categorization, Generation, Debugging, Refinement); the Generation, Debugging and Refinement agents each consult their own Memory module, an offline-profiled ranking matrix indexed by (programming language, algorithmic category), to select the top-k=5 candidate LLMs most suitable for that specific stage/task at runtime, applying stage-specific acceptance criteria and correctness-preserving rollback if a chosen model's attempt fails.
evaluacion: HumanEval-X and EffiBench-X (2,500 problems, 5 languages) with 5 LLMs, comparing PerfOrch against single-model pipelines (PerfCodeGen-GPT-4o), majority voting, and exhaustive multi-model evaluation; a preliminary 3-model study (Tables 1-3) establishes the per-stage/per-category routing premise, and Memory built solely on HumanEval-X profiling is evaluated zero-shot on the unseen EffiBench-X benchmark.
numeros_clave: PerfOrch average pass@1 97.19% (HumanEval-X) / 95.83% (EffiBench-X), +1.22 to +14.58pp over the strongest single-model pipeline; per-stage pairing reaches 98.17%/85.98% (Python/Rust) vs majority voting 97.56%/84.76%; category-aware routing adds +2.43pp on Rust (88.41% vs 85.98%); execution time improved for 61-90% of solved problems with mean speedups 4.7-29.9%, at roughly half the token cost of exhaustive multi-model evaluation.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Each agent's Memory is a per-(language,category) ranking matrix built from OFFLINE profiling and consulted, not re-derived, at runtime to pick which model to trust for a given task -- an alternative measured-retrieval pattern operating over model-performance priors rather than documents.

PerfOrch matches the refinement coverage of exhaustive multi-model evaluation 'at roughly half the token cost' (abstract) and bounds overhead via a top-k=5 candidate pool chosen from a measured plateau (Section 6.2 sensitivity analysis), concrete evidence that a small measured cache beats brute-force redundancy.

The ranking Memory is described as 'updatable as new models/versions become available' (Section 3.2), but the paper does not evaluate an online-consolidation mechanism, so this is a stated design intent rather than measured evidence.

notes: Tables 1-3 (preliminary 3-model study) and the abstract's headline numbers (97.19%/95.83% pass@1, 4.7-29.9% speedups) anchor the figures; 'Memory' here is model-performance-ranking metadata, not task/user knowledge -- a narrower notion of memory than most other papers in this batch.

cita: Fang et al. (2025). MLZero: A Multi-Agent System for End-to-end Machine Learning Automation.
problema: End-to-end multimodal AutoML agents lack automated data perception (forcing hard-coded preprocessing) and, when relying solely on parametric knowledge, hallucinate code or use outdated ML-library APIs; their performance further degrades when managing long, convoluted domain knowledge without efficient memory mechanisms.
mecanismo: MLZero pairs a perception module (file-grouping/perception, task-perception and ML-library-selection agents) with dual memory: semantic memory is built OFFLINE by summarization and condensation agents into queryable, condensed per-library knowledge indices, then retrieved at each iteration conditioned on the current error context to supply targeted guidance; episodic memory maintains a chronological record of prior code, execution logs, retrieved knowledge and error context per iteration, distilled by an error-analyzer agent into a concise error summary plus fix suggestion, feeding an iterative coder-executer loop until success or a max-iteration limit.
evaluacion: MLE-Bench Lite (21 Kaggle competitions) and a new Multimodal AutoML Agent Benchmark (25 datasets, diverse modalities) against AIDE, DS-Agent, AutoKaggle and Codex CLI, with ablations removing external knowledge (semantic memory, -ext) and episodic memory (-epi), plus a compact 8B-LLM robustness variant.
numeros_clave: MLE-Bench Lite: 86% success rate / avg rank 1.43 vs AIDE 81%/2.36, with 6 gold + 2 silver medals; Multimodal benchmark: success rate 0.92 (+263.6% vs the best baseline), avg rank 2.42; the compact-8B variant still reaches 45.3% success / rank 5.14, beating other agents' full-size configurations (Table 1).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Semantic memory is explicitly built OFFLINE (summarization+condensation agents) as a derived, queryable index over library documentation/tutorials, then retrieved per-iteration, a clean instance of MF's derived-index-as-cache (Tier-3) pattern.

Episodic memory explicitly distills raw execution history into a concise error-summary-plus-fix-suggestion rather than replaying full logs, stated to reduce token consumption while preserving problem-solving effectiveness (Section 3.3), directly supporting MF's context-economy stance.

An ablation explicitly measures the contribution of external-knowledge retrieval (-ext) and episodic memory (-epi) to end-to-end success rate (Table 1), evidence that retrieval/memory presence is measurably load-bearing rather than assumed.

notes: Table 1 (25-dataset Multimodal AutoML benchmark, -ext/-epi ablation columns) and the MLE-Bench Lite medal counts anchor the numbers; industry paper (AWS/Amazon authors) with a fully public benchmark and repository.

cita: Tablan et al. (2025). Smarter Together: Creating Agentic Communities of Practice through Shared Experiential Learning.
problema: The shift to agent-centric software development is eroding human developer knowledge-sharing communities (falling participation in peer repositories), while AI coding agents remain siloed and amnesiac -- each session, user, or provider starts a fresh, isolated learning loop with no equivalent shared 'community of practice' to draw on.
mecanismo: Spark is a shared, multi-agent-writable experiential memory layer with three subsystems: a knowledge base (seeded by indexing raw developer documentation across text/embedding modalities), a retrieval agent (an 8-step workflow: intent analysis -> search-strategy planning -> recall of past experiential traces -> documentation retrieval -> recommendation generation -> citation -> best-practice synthesis -> contextualized response) combining vector search, lexical search and experiential-trace matching, and a continuous multi-epoch experiential-learning loop that captures every agent interaction as a structured 'trace,' clusters and curates traces into generalizable knowledge patterns each epoch, and redistributes that curated knowledge to future agents facing similar problems.
evaluacion: DS-1000 (1000 Python data-science problems from StackOverflow, 7 libraries) with three codegen backbones (Qwen3-Coder-30B, Claude Haiku 4.5, GPT-5-Codex) compared NO-SPARK vs WITH-SPARK (one epoch of synthetic experiential-trace ingestion), judged by an independent LLM (Gemini 2.5 Pro) on a 5-point code-quality scale across correctness/completeness/code-quality/practicality, plus a separate helpfulness-band evaluation of Spark's recommendations.
numeros_clave: WITH-SPARK raises mean code quality for all three backbones (Fig.1); a 30B open-weights model boosted by Spark matches the code quality of a much larger SOTA model; Spark recommendation helpfulness reaches up to 98.2% in the top-two of five qualitative bands; knowledge base seeded with approximately 34,000 documentation blobs.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: A continuous multi-epoch curation loop (feedback -> knowledge extraction -> memory-augmented learning -> next epoch, Section 3.2) that clusters raw interaction traces into generalizable 'curated knowledge' distinct from the raw traces themselves is a directly transferable pattern for promoting gotchas into durable recipes.

Spark is explicitly framed as a SHARED cross-agent/cross-user memory versus today's siloed single-user provider- or user-managed memory stores (Sections 2.1-2.2), a concrete alternative to per-agent private stores directly engaging MF's single-source/multi-store-seams question.

The paper does not detail how conflicting or stale curated knowledge is reconciled or aged out across a large multi-agent contributor base, leaving MF's provenance/staleness/poisoning concern for a genuinely shared memory largely unaddressed by the evaluation.

notes: Fig.1 (code quality by backbone) and Section 4.4-4.5 (helpfulness bands, 98.2% figure) anchor the numbers; industry paper (The Memory Company / Moonsong Labs) evaluated only with SYNTHETIC experiential traces from one LLM (Section 4.1) rather than real multi-agent/multi-user community usage -- RECONSIDERAR how far the 'shared community' claim is validated versus a single-epoch synthetic proxy.
